title: [CVSS 8.1 HIGH] CVE-2026-85736 — Chartbrew is an open-source web application that can connect directly to databas…
summary: Chartbrew is an open-source web application that can connect directly to databases and APIs and use the data to create charts. The vulnerable surface is data-connection certificate and SSH-key cleanup when a connection is removed. A user with createOwn and deleteOwn permissions on their own team stores a target path in a connection and then deletes the connection to trigger cleanup; default self-signup grants teamOwner these permissions. The cleanup routine treats the stored SSL or SSH path as a managed certificate path and unlinks the referenced file; duplicateConnection provides a second advisory-identified trigger. The attacker must be able to create or update and then delete a connection on their own team. The default container runs Chartbrew as uid 0, while deployments with a less-privileged process are limited by that process's deletion permissions. The attacker can delete files such as /code/.env or application source, causing integrity loss and service disruption. This issue is fixed in version 5.2.3.

title: [CVSS 8.8 HIGH] CVE-2026-85712 — Chartbrew is an open-source web application that can connect directly to databas…

An authenticated user who is an owner or admin of their own team submits a victim project id together with the attacker's own team_id in the request body; default self-signup grants the required role on the user's own team. Authorization is evaluated against the attacker-selected team instead of the target project's team, and the update path mass-assigns the request body without a project field allow-list. The attacker needs a valid Chartbrew account, an owner or admin role on their own team, and a victim project identifier; requests without the body team_id trick are rejected. title: [CVSS 9.8 CRITICAL] CVE-2026-85295 — Chartbrew is an open-source web application that can connect directly to databas…
